packet-16 - first blind reading (unverified image reading)

Exposure note: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this packet. A paper/archive shelfmark label pencilled on the leaf is visible in the overviews ("Stams, STA, Frag. 128-2r" on image-021, "...128-2v" on image-031); I note it only as a visible inscription.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overviews image-001, -011, -021, -031)
- Four overviews, each followed by nine native-resolution tiles (apparently a 3x3 grid: top-left, top-centre, top-right, middle row, bottom row): 001 -> 002-010; 011 -> 012-020; 021 -> 022-030; 031 -> 032-040.
- One damaged sheet of parchment, landscape, reused (folded edges: a folded strip at the bottom, folded strips at left and right, torn top edge; tape repairs). Looks like a binding wrapper / cover. Fold lines also vertical down the middle.
- Writing in long lines, not columns; a documentary-looking German-style cursive (charter/chancery hand), brown ink. No rubrics or enlarged initials seen in the overviews.
- image-011 face: ~28-30 long lines visible across the whole width, with text running onto the right folded flap (lines continue past a fold). Darker, more legible than 001/021. Blue/grey pencil note "...trich"? at upper left margin (modern).
- image-031 face: ~30 long lines, text also on the left flap; lower lines darker; lowest lines on the bottom fold partly hidden by a grey redaction box. Top-right area shows offset/stuck-on printed or written text (mirror?) on damaged patches.
- image-001 and image-021 faces: text extremely faint (washed / abraded, maybe the outer side of the wrapper); ruled long lines visible; frame ruling seen. Bottom strip of 021 has a faint line of writing.
- Tentative: the sheet carries a single continuous documentary text (letter/charter) in German; the 011 and 031 faces may be the same side across folds or the two sides. I do not infer more.

TRANSCRIPTIONS
(Line numbers count from the top of each tile image. Expansions in parentheses; ? = uncertain.)

== image-012 (face of overview 011, top-left tile; also crop-01.jpg = blue-channel contrast crop of its text area) ==
Hand: fast late cursive (German vernacular appears likely from word shapes "das", "Dem", "man"), ink much faded and smeared; left text edge marked by a vertical ruled line with a dark ink tick at the top. Modern pencil in left margin: "Vlrich" (bluish pencil, upper-left margin, at level of text lines 5-6).
